data.title: Rates Are Shifting: Gift a CD That Locks In At Least 5.10% APY Before Year-End
data.description:
Rates Are Shifting: Gift a CD That Locks In At Least 5.10% APY Before Year-End

Rates Are Shifting: Gift a CD That Locks In At Least 5.10% APY Before Year-End

PR Newswire

SEATTLE, Nov. 23, 2026

With top CD rates at 5.10% APY and higher, CDs offer a low-risk, federally insured way to give to kids, grandkids and the causes you care about

SEATTLE, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Money has become one of the most popular holiday gifts, and this year there's a smarter way to give it. Nearly 72% of parents and grandparents give the gift of green during the holidays, according to a YouGov survey conducted for CD Valet. Certificates of deposit turn that cash into a gift that grows with steady returns.

With top CD rates currently at 5.10% APY and higher (as of November 22), gift givers can lock in a rate today and watch their gift grow. CDs can be gifted to children through a custodial account, or to a charity by opening a CD in its name, naming it as a beneficiary, or donating the interest.

Financial Gifts Go Mainstream and CDs Stand Out

Parents and grandparents say they give money for its convenience and ease (66%), to avoid unwanted gifts and returns (45%), and because the recipient has immediate financial needs (28%). Monetary gifts (72%) outrank personal technology gifts (55%).

Most financial gifts are for the here and now, but 32% of givers focus on longer-term investments. Among those who give investments, 55% want to support their family's future financial security, and 43% want to teach family members about investing and financial planning.

"Cash used to be considered the fallback holiday gift for people who didn't like to shop but not anymore," said Mary Grace Roske, Head of Communications for CD Valet. "In just one week, the number of CDs paying more than 5.00% APY has climbed, making it easy for gift givers to lock in a competitive rate. It's the smart gift that's worth more than the day you gave it."

Where CD Rates Stand This Holiday Season

According to CD Valet data, the top CD rate offered by federally insured banks is 5.10% APY for a 60-month CD. The current top rate offered by NCUA-insured credit unions is a limited balance promotional offer of 9.00% APY for a 9-month CD. The median rate across all terms is 3.39% APY, compared with 3.30% APY at the end of last month.

Top-tier rates are climbing heading into the holidays. Over the past 30 days, top 1% rates rose to 4.40% APY for 6-month CDs (from 4.35%), 4.55% APY for 12-month CDs (from 4.50%) and 4.58% APY for 24-month CDs (from 4.50%). Median rates also edged up, with 12-month CDs at 3.42% APY (up 2 bps) and 24-month CDs at 3.20% APY (up 1 bps).

How to Gift a CD

For kids and grandkids:

  • Open a custodial CD. Parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles and friends can open a CD for a child through a custodial account. Any adult 18 or older can serve as custodian and oversee the account until the child reaches the age of majority.
  • Shop for competitive rates. Look for banks or credit unions that offer competitive CD rates and clear custodial options. Online platforms like CD Valet compare rates nationwide to help you find the best promotional CDs for your gift.
  • Gather your documents. Most institutions ask for the child's Social Security number, birth date, and a school ID or passport if available, plus the adult's U.S. ID and Social Security number. Confirm exact requirements with the institution.

For nonprofit organizations:

There are a few ways you can choose to donate a CD to a non-profit:

  • Open a CD in the nonprofit's name. You'll need the organization's tax ID number and approval, proof of authorization on official letterhead or in its bylaws, its organization documents, and identification for its authorized signers.
  • Name a charity as your CD's Payable on Death (POD) beneficiary. You stay in control during your lifetime, and the account passes to the charity without your executor needing to act.
  • Donate at maturity. Lock in a rate and term, let the principal grow to your target amount, then donate.

Rules to Know Before You Gift

  • Custodial gifts are permanent. CDs opened under the Uniform Gifts to Minors Act (UGMA) or Uniform Transfers to Minors Act (UTMA) are irrevocably gifted to the child. Before adulthood, the funds can be used only in the child's best interest, such as buying a car or getting an apartment.
  • Deposit insurance has limits. CDs opened at an FDIC-insured bank are insured up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category, and the limit covers principal plus accrued interest. Credit union CDs, called share certificates, carry the same $250,000 protection from the NCUA. Naming an IRS-qualified individual, organization or nonprofit as a POD beneficiary qualifies for FDIC coverage up to $250,000.
  • Check with the nonprofit organization first. Ask the organization directly whether it accepts CDs opened on its behalf before you start.
  • Charitable gifts may be tax deductible. Consult a qualified tax advisor regarding your specific situation.

CD Valet tracks around 40,000 publicly listed CD rates from nearly 5,000 banks and credit unions across the country. Visit https://www.cdvalet.com/insights/cd-rate-forecast/ for the full report on where CD rates are headed in 2026.

About CD Valet

CD Valet is a CD marketplace that features verified CD rates from federally insured banks and credit unions. With tens of thousands of CD offers tracked across the country, CD Valet gives savers a clear view of top rates and helps them explore high-yield CD options with reliable returns. For financial institutions looking to raise deposits and attract new customers, CD Valet is a reliable and cost-effective channel that helps boost the visibility of their brand and CD offerings to high-intent CD customers. Visit www.cdvalet.com for more information and check out CD Valet's Best CD Rates for today's highest offerings.

data.title: Sexual Harassment Lawsuit Against Channel 4 "Virgin Island" Experts Moves Toward Trial
data.description:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 23, 2026 / A civil lawsuit involving sexual harassment and workplace retaliation claims is moving toward a February 2027 trial in the Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco, according to public court filings in Brockman v. Somatica LLC, et al. (Case No. CGC-24-618718).

Margo Brockman. Photo courtesy of Margo Brockman.

The lawsuit, filed by former marketing and business development executive Margo Brockman against Somatica LLC and its founders, Danielle Harel and Celeste Hirschman-who serve as lead experts and co-executive producers on the Channel 4 series Virgin Island-includes claims under California Civil Code Section 51.9, the Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), California Labor Code Section 1102.5, and breach of contract.

The case remains pending in San Francisco Superior Court, with trial currently scheduled for February 2027.

data.title: Hugel marks 25th anniversary with global medical and academic exchange
data.description:
Hugel marks 25th anniversary with global medical and academic exchange

Hugel marks 25th anniversary with global medical and academic exchange

PR Newswire

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 23, 2026
  • "2026 H.E.L.F. in Seoul" concludes November 21–23 as Hugel's largest-ever global academic event
  • The program draws approximately 400 medical professionals from Korea and abroad for clinic tours, a symposium and a factory tour

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hugel Inc., a leading global medical aesthetics company publicly traded in South Korea, hosted its largest-ever global medical symposium, "2026 H.E.L.F. in Seoul," from November 21 to 23 to celebrate the 25th anniversary of its founding. The event brought together medical professionals from Korea and abroad to share the company's 25 years of expertise in product development, academic research and manufacturing.

H.E.L.F., or Hugel Expert Leader's Forum, is the company's flagship global symposium that has been held since 2013. This year's theme was "Beauty in Harmony," focusing on understanding beauty standards and treatment trends across countries and exploring ways to achieve harmony amid those differences. The program included clinic visits, a symposium and a tour of Hugel's production facilities, giving participants an opportunity to gain firsthand insights into the medical aesthetics field, from clinical practice to product manufacturing.

On November 21, the company organized visits to 11 leading clinics across Korea for approximately 200 international medical professionals, who participated in educational lectures and live demonstrations. At one of the clinics, Dr. Seung-ju Lee of The Other Dermatology Clinic demonstrated combination treatment techniques using Hugel's diverse product portfolio, giving participants a practical understanding of the latest K-aesthetics trends through live demonstrations.

The gala dinner that evening was moderated by Dr. Hee-dae Jeon of Banobagi Dermatologic Clinic. The session in the evening featured presentations on treatment strategies shaped by aesthetic trends in different markets. Speakers included Dr. Wook Oh of Maylin Clinic The Hyundai Seoul, Dr. Min-seong Kim of Inee Clinic and four international healthcare professionals (HCPs).

The academic symposium took place on November 22, Hugel's founding anniversary, with approximately 400 medical professionals from Korea and overseas in attendance. Hyesung Kim, a professor at Incheon St. Mary's Hospital, moderated the symposium by highlighting key takeaways from the presentations and leading the discussions. Before the main sessions, Haiyan Cui, a professor at Tongji Hospital of Tongji University, introduced the event's theme of "harmony" and its significance in medical aesthetics.

Speakers from Korea and abroad explored the same topics from different regional perspectives, sharing valuable perspectives for clinical practice. The session focused on botulinum toxin treatment strategies tailored to differences between Eastern and Western patients and between male and female patients. The presentations were delivered by Dr. Nark-kyoung Rho of Leaders Dermatology Clinic Cheongdam and Dr. Hyun-jo Kim of CNP Dermatology Clinic Cheonan-Asan Station, alongside two German HCPs, Dr. Mirko Matthias Fuchs of Belstetica Private Clinic and Dr. Konstantin Frank of Lvate Face Aesthetics.

Another presentation focused on HA filler treatment strategies for addressing "Ozempic face," a condition characterized by facial volume loss and skin laxity following rapid weight loss associated with obesity medications. The presentation was delivered by Dr. Choon-shik Yoon of Yemiwon Dermatology Clinic. Other presentations covered combination treatment approaches incorporating botulinum toxin, HA fillers, and skin rejuvenation.

On November 23, Hugel hosted a factory tour in Chuncheon, Gangwon State for approximately 200 international HCPs. Participants toured the facilities and learned about Hugel's manufacturing capabilities and quality management systems developed over the past 25 years. The tour also offered an overview of the manufacturing processes behind the products featured in the symposium's academic sessions and clinical demonstrations.

"As Hugel marks its 25th anniversary, it is especially meaningful to reflect on our achievements and discuss the path forward at '2026 H.E.L.F. in Seoul' with medical professionals from Korea and around the world who have been part of our growth journey," said Daniel Chang, Korea CEO of Hugel. "We will continue to expand academic exchange and educational programs grounded in clinical evidence for medical professionals, while contributing to the advancement of the global medical aesthetics industry."

About Hugel

Established in 2001, Hugel is a global leader in medical aesthetics, specializing in the production of injectables for skin rejuvenation, including botulinum toxin, hyaluronic acid dermal fillers, and skinboosters, as well as absorbable sutures and cosmetic products. With a proven track record of safety and quality, Hugel is deeply committed to advancing the industry through robust medical affairs, comprehensive training programs, and dynamic industry forums.

Over the past 25 years, the company has built a presence in approximately 70 countries and operates 11 global subsidiaries across the U.S., Australia, Canada, Taiwan region, China, Hong Kong SAR, Singapore, Thailand, and New Zealand. Leveraging strong industry momentum, Hugel is well-positioned for continued growth and market expansion worldwide.

SharkNinja Set to Join S&P 500; Others to Join S&P MidCap 400 and S&P SmallCap 600

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- S&P Dow Jones Indices will make the following changes to the S&P 500, S&P MidCap 400, S&P SmallCap 600: 

  • S&P MidCap 400 constituent SharkNinja Inc. (NYSE: SN) will replace AES Corp. (NYSE: AES) in the S&P 500, S&P SmallCap 600 constituent Paycom Software Inc. (NYSE: PAYC) will replace SharkNinja in the S&P MidCap 400, and Guardian Pharmacy Services Inc. (NYSE: GRDN) will replace Paycom Software in the S&P SmallCap 600 effective prior to the opening of trading on Wednesday, December 2. A consortium, including Global Infrastructure Partners and EQT Infrastructure, are acquiring AES in a deal expected to be completed soon pending final conditions.

Blackstone Infrastructure Portfolio Company and Safe Harbor are acquiring MarineMax in a deal expected to close soon, pending final closing conditions.

data.title: Strathcona Resources and Greenfire Resources Announce Filing of Joint Management Information Circular and Receipt of Interim Order
data.description:
Strathcona Resources and Greenfire Resources Announce Filing of Joint Management Information Circular and Receipt of Interim Order

Strathcona Resources and Greenfire Resources Announce Filing of Joint Management Information Circular and Receipt of Interim Order

PR Newswire

CALGARY, AB, Nov. 23, 2026

CALGARY, AB, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Strathcona Resources Ltd. ("Strathcona") (TSX: SCR) and Greenfire Resources Ltd. ("Greenfire") (TSX: GFR) (NYSE: GFR) are pleased to jointly announce that Strathcona and Greenfire obtained an interim order of the Court of King's Bench earlier today, November 23, 2026, and have each filed the joint management information circular (the "Joint Circular") dated November 23, 2026 and related meeting and proxy materials in connection with the proposed arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (the "Arrangement"). The Arrangement provides for, among other matters, the acquisition by Strathcona of all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Greenfire pursuant to the arrangement agreement between Strathcona and Greenfire dated effective November 8, 2026.

The meeting materials will be mailed shortly to holders of common shares of each of Strathcona ("Strathcona Shareholders") and Greenfire ("Greenfire Shareholders", and together with Strathcona Shareholders, "Shareholders") of record as of November 23, 2026. The Joint Circular, as well as the Schedule 13E-3 transaction statement (which includes the Joint Circular and related proxy materials), is available under each of Strathcona and Greenfire's SEDAR+ profiles at www.sedarplus.ca and on Greenfire's EDGAR profile at www.sec.gov, as well as on their respective websites, at https://www.strathconaresources.com and https://www.greenfireres.com.

Special Meeting Details

Strathcona will hold a special meeting (the "Strathcona Meeting") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 10:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP, Suite 3500, 855 – 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4J8. Greenfire will hold a special meeting (the "Greenfire Meeting" and, together with the Strathcona Meeting, the "Meetings") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 9:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Bennett Jones LLP, Suite 4500, 855 – 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4K7.

The boards of directors of Strathcona and Greenfire have each unanimously recommended their minority Shareholders vote for the applicable Arrangement resolution.

Shareholders are encouraged to vote well in advance of the Meetings, whether or not a Shareholder is intending to attend the Meetings in person. Details on how to vote can be found in the Joint Circular under the sections "General Information Concerning The Strathcona Meeting And Voting" and "General Information Concerning The Greenfire Meeting And Voting". Voting will open immediately following the mailing of the meeting materials, expected to be on or about December 1, 2026.

Strathcona and Greenfire have each retained Laurel Hill Advisory Group ("Laurel Hill") as its proxy solicitation agent in connection with the Meetings. Shareholders with questions or who require assistance voting are encouraged to contact Laurel Hill by calling 1 877 452 7184 (toll free in North America) or +1 416 304 0211 (outside North America), texting "INFO" to either number, or by emailing assistance@laurelhill.com.

About Strathcona

Strathcona is one of North America's fastest growing pure play heavy oil producers with operations focused on thermal oil and enhanced oil recovery. Strathcona is built on an innovative approach to growth achieved through the consolidation and development of long-life assets. Strathcona's common shares (symbol SCR) are listed on the TSX.

For more information about Strathcona, visit www.strathconaresources.com.

About Greenfire

Greenfire is an oil sands producer actively developing its long-life and low-decline thermal oil assets in the Athabasca region of Alberta, Canada, with its registered office in Calgary, Alberta. Greenfire plans to leverage its large resource base and significant infrastructure in place to drive meaningful, capital-efficient production growth. Greenfire common shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Toronto Stock Exchange under the trading symbol "GFR".

data.title: The newest addition to the S&P 500 is a maker of viral ice-cream machines
data.description:
By Claudia Assis

SharkNinja will join the S&P 500, replacing AES

SharkNinja will be replacing a utility and power company in the benchmark index.

SharkNinja, maker of several small-appliance products that have gone viral in recent years, such as the Ninja Creami ice-cream maker and the Ninja Crispi air fryer, is joining the S&P 500 index.

The latest move from S&P Dow Jones Indices, announced Monday, is a departure from recent inclusions, which have tended to favor tech companies. The consumer-products brand will replace utility and power generator AES (AES) on Dec. 2, the index provider said. A consortium is buying AES in a deal expected to close soon.

Shares of SharkNinja (SN) rose nearly 2% in the after-hours session Monday after ending the regular trading day up 6%. The company went public in 2023.

Recent S&P 500 SPX shake-ups included the inclusion of Twilio (TWLO) in October, as well as the addition of chip maker Marvell Technology (MRVL) and electronics manufacturer Flex (FLEX) earlier this year. The index also added Ferguson (FERG), a wholesale distributor of plumbing, heating and other products for construction trades, in July.

A spot in the S&P 500 is a coveted place for companies, as it brings their shares to a much broader range of investors, including passive funds that track indexes and actively managed funds that may have limitations on where they can invest.

More S&P 500 changes could be announced next Friday as the index committee conducts its quarterly rebalancing.

-Claudia Assis

data.title: First Day Introduces First-of-Its-Kind 8-in-1 Protein + Fiber + Collagen Ready-To-Pour Liquid Packets for the Whole Family
data.description:
First Day Introduces First-of-Its-Kind 8-in-1 Protein + Fiber + Collagen Ready-To-Pour Liquid Packets for the Whole Family

First Day Introduces First-of-Its-Kind 8-in-1 Protein + Fiber + Collagen Ready-To-Pour Liquid Packets for the Whole Family

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026

The family nutrition brand reimagines traditional protein and fiber supplements with an innovative ready-to-pour liquid format combining complete protein, five sources of fiber, and collagen in one convenient liquid packet.

NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, First Day announces the first-of-its-kind Ready-to-Pour Protein + Fiber + Collagen 8-in-1 Complex Liquid Packets, marking a major expansion beyond its signature gummies into functional nutrition.

 First Day launches a ready-to-pour liquid packet combining complete protein, five sources of fiber, and collagen

Available in age-specific formulas for kids, teens, and adults, the new complex introduces an unparalleled liquid format that combines complete protein for muscle health, a 5-fiber blend for digestive support, and in the teens and adults formulas, VERISOL® Bioactive Collagen Peptides, clinically studied to improve skin elasticity, boost hydration, and visibly reduce fine lines and wrinkles. VERISOL® is specifically developed to support the skin's natural collagen production, delivering clinically studied beauty-from-within benefits in as little as eight weeks. Together, these ingredients create an innovative 3-in-1 formula designed to help close common nutritional gaps and support everyday wellness for the whole family.

The new Ready-to-Pour liquid packets were developed to address common frustrations with traditional protein and fiber supplements. According to a recent 2026 consumer study, 84% of moms surveyed said protein powders clump, while 82% found liquid packets more appealing than traditional powders, shakes, and tubs.* Additionally, more than 90% of U.S. adults fall short of their daily fiber target, further highlighting the need for convenient ways to support daily nutrition.

Powered by First Day's innovative Bio-Liquid Technology, the formula features active ingredients that come already dissolved, eliminating the clumping and gritty residue commonly associated with traditional protein powders. Each ready-to-pour packet mixes directly into water, offering a simpler alternative to traditional powders and shakes, with no scooping or blending required.

The new Ready-to-Pour Protein + Fiber + Collagen Liquid Packets feature age-specific formulations, including:

  • Kids (Ages 4–12): 6g of protein, 4g of fiber, and bioactive collagen peptides to support growth, daily nutrition, digestive health, and healthy bone development.
  • Teens (Ages 13–17): 10g of protein, 7g of fiber, and 2.5g of VERISOL® collagen to support muscle health, digestion, and healthy hair, skin, and nails.
  • Adults (Ages 18+): 15g of protein, 8g of fiber, and 2.5g of VERISOL® collagen peptides to support muscle health, digestive wellness, skin elasticity, and visibly reduced fine lines and wrinkles.

Available in Peach Mango and Lemonade flavors, the new Ready-to-Pour Liquid Packets are offered in 15-count packs for $49.00. 8-count packs will debut at Target stores in late December for $29.99. Pricing varies by retailer.

"We've always believed that better nutrition should be simple and accessible for the whole family," said Alice Li, Founder and CEO of First Day. "With Ready-to-Pour, we're reaching beyond gummies to make everyday wellness even easier, without compromising on the quality and science-backed approach families expect from First Day."

i-80 Gold Announces the Start of Production Mining at Archimedes Underground

i-80 Gold Announces the Start of Production Mining at Archimedes Underground

PR Newswire

TORONTO, Nov. 23, 2026

All amounts are expressed in United States dollars unless otherwise stated

TORONTO, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- i-80 GOLD CORP. (NYSE: IAUX) (TSX: IAU) ("i-80 Gold", or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has mined its first gold and commenced production mining on schedule at its Archimedes underground project ("Archimedes" or the "Project"). Archimedes is a high-grade gold project located on the Company's Ruby Hill property within the Battle Mountain-Eureka gold trend in Nevada, USA. It is the Company's second underground mine to come online.

"The start of production mining at Archimedes marks another significant step for i-80 Gold, further strengthening our track record of delivering on key development milestones," stated Paul Chawrun, Executive Vice President & Chief Operating Officer. "We are currently mining oxide and sulfide material at the Project. The oxide material is being placed on the active heap leach pad on the Ruby Hill property, while the sulfide material is being stockpiled for processing at our Lone Tree Plant next year. Our strong technical and operating teams and our underground mining contractor have enabled us to deliver on this milestone safely, on time and largely on budget."

Mr. Chawrun added, "Our focus for the Project now turns to ramping up mining rates through 2027 and stockpiling the refractory material mined in preparation for the commissioning of the Lone Tree Plant late in the year as Archimedes will be a key source of high-grade refractory material feed. Once the Lone Tree Plant is commissioned, we are targeting consolidated annual gold production of 150,000 to 200,000 ounces beginning in 2028 from the Archimedes and Granite Creek underground projects."(1) 

Project Development

Production mining commenced following the scheduled completion of the surface and underground infrastructure required to begin production mining, including ventilation and escape raises. Lateral development to date totals approximately 3,600 meters. Ground conditions remain favorable, and the underground contractor continues to exceed planned productivity rates within the Project's upper 426 Zone. Construction of additional surface and underground infrastructure, such as additional ventilation raises, a permanent mine dry, and offices, will continue through 2027 to support the ramp up to planned mining rates. 

Project construction commenced in September 2025 and has progressed largely in line with the capital development estimate in the March 2025 preliminary economic assessment (the "PEA"),(2) apart from the decision to expand and upgrade surface infrastructure to support the scale of future operations. Upon anticipated completion of the additional surface and underground infrastructure in 2027, total project capital is expected to be approximately $10 million higher than the $47.3 million estimated in the PEA.

Processing and Stockpiling 

Archimedes is a high-grade gold project consisting of sulfide (refractory) mineralized material as well as oxide mineralized material predominately in the upper 426 Zone. The recently completed 2025-2026 drilling program for the upper 426 Zone intersected significant intervals of oxide mineralization outside the mineral resource estimate contained in the PEA (refer to the Company's press release dated June 25, 2026). Metallurgical test work results have confirmed that the oxide material is amenable to heap leaching on the Ruby Hill property at lower overall processing costs compared to processing through the Company's oxide mill circuit at the Lone Tree Plant.

Beginning in mid-November, oxide material mined from the upper 426 Zone was placed on the existing heap leach pad on the Ruby Hill property, and the Company expects to begin recovering the associated gold in the first quarter of 2027.

Mining development rates at Archimedes are progressing faster than outlined in the PEA and moreover, the Company expects the majority of the mineralized material mined in 2027 to be oxide and to be placed on the existing heap leach pad. While the PEA assumed some tonnage being placed on the leach pad in 2027, the majority of the mineralized material mined was expected to be sulfide and toll milled at a 58% payability factor. Given the Company believes a majority of the mined mineralized material in 2027 to be oxide, it is expected that the Company will be able to increase its heap leach production outlook.(3) Full guidance will be provided early in the new year.

As previously disclosed, in 2027 the Company expects to stockpile all refractory material mined at Archimedes, along with a large portion of oxide and refractory material mined at Granite Creek underground. The stockpiled material is intended to be processed at the Company's wholly owned Lone Tree Plant upon its planned commissioning in the fourth quarter of 2027, rather than processed at a third-party facility. Additionally, over the next three years a significant portion of mineralized material mined at the Project is expected to be oxide and placed on the Ruby Hill leach pad.

2027 Planned Feasibility Study

Drilling in the upper 426 Zone was completed in April 2026. Drilling in the lower 426 and Ruby Deeps zones commenced in the second quarter of 2026. Seven underground drill rigs are currently active on site targeting approximately 55,000 meters planned across 140 drill holes. The drilling campaign is expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2027 and is designed to evaluate extensions to the mineralized system and enhance resource definition to support the Archimedes feasibility study, which is planned for completion in the second half of 2027.(2)

As of December 31, 2025, Archimedes hosts an Indicated Mineral Resource of 1.8 million tonnes containing 436,000 ounces of gold grading 7.6 grams per tonne and an Inferred Mineral Resource of 4.2 million tonnes containing 988,000 ounces of gold grading 7.3 grams per tonne.(4) The majority of the current Mineral Resource Estimate is hosted in the Ruby Deeps Zone, located below the 5,100-foot elevation of the deposit as demonstrated in the Figure below.

Technical Disclosure and Qualified Person

The technical information contained in this press release has been prepared under the supervision of, and has been reviewed and approved by Paul Chawrun P.Eng., Executive Vice President & Chief Operating Officer, for the Company, who is a qualified person within the meaning of National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101") and Subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended ("S-K 1300"). Mr. Chawrun has verified the scientific and technical information disclosed in this press release.

Endnotes

(1)

Based on gold output estimates in the most recent life of mine gold output schedules disclosed in the latest technical studies filed for each respective project and related property: Granite Creek underground, Archimedes underground, Cove underground, and Mineral Point open pit. These anticipated output figures are preliminary in nature and are largely based on mineral resources, which do not have demonstrated economic viability and subject to successful project development. Only Granite Creek underground has declared mineral reserves. In addition, for all gold projects except Granite Creek underground, the foregoing technical reports are preliminary economic assessments/initial assessments that are preliminary in nature. The Granite Creek underground technical report was a feasibility study/technical report summary.  Each include an economic analysis that is based, in part, on inferred mineral resources. Inferred mineral resources are considered too speculative geologically to have economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as mineral reserves. As such, there is no certainty that the output targets will be realized. Anticipated output targets are also pending the commissioning of the Lone Tree Plant and are Company goals and not a projection of results and should not be taken as output guidance. All of the Company's projects other than Granite Creek underground are considered exploration stage projects under S-K 1300, as the Company has not determined mineral reserves at such properties pursuant to S-K 1300. With respect to Archimedes underground, located on the Ruby Hill property, the Company has started extraction activities without determining mineral reserves. The following technical reports for each project and related property have been prepared in accordance with NI 43-101: Preliminary Economic Assessment Technical Report for the Cove Project, Lander County, Nevada (March 31, 2025); NI 43-101 Technical Report Feasibility Study Granite Creek, Humboldt County, Nevada, USA (September 21, 2026); and Preliminary Economic Assessment NI 43-101 Technical Report for the Ruby Hill Project, Eureka County Nevada, USA (March 31, 2025). Corresponding technical reports prepared in accordance with S-K 1300 are as follows: Initial Assessment & Technical Report Summary for the Cove Project, Lander County, Nevada (March 26, 2025); S-K 1300 SEC Technical Report Summary Pre-Feasibility Study Granite Creek, Humboldt County, NV (September 21, 2026); and Initial Assessment of the Ruby Hill Project, Eureka County NV (March 29, 2025).

(2)

See the discussion of the Archimedes Underground project in the Company's S-K 1300 Technical Report Summary, Initial Assessment for the Ruby Hill Complex, Eureka County, Nevada effective December 31, 2024 in the Form 8-K dated March 31, 2025. The PEA was prepared in accordance with NI 43-101 and the corresponding Initial Assessment prepared under S-K 1300 and item 601 of the Regulation S-K, each filed on SEDAR+ and EDGAR, respectively, on March 31, 2025. The planned feasibility study is expected to be prepared under both: NI 43-101 which, in the opinion of the qualified persons, constitutes a feasibility study; and S-K 1300 which, in the opinion of the qualified persons, constitutes a pre-feasibility study.

(3)

The oxide mineralized material mined and expected to be mined at Archimedes includes material that, as previously disclosed, is outside the mineral resource estimate supporting the PEA and has not been classified as mineral resources or mineral reserves. The Company is not providing an estimate of the quantity or grade of this material at this time, and its contribution to heap leach production will depend on the results of mining and leaching.

About i-80 Gold Corp.

i-80 Gold Corp. is a Nevada-focused mining company committed to building a mid-tier gold producer through a funded development plan to advance its high-quality asset portfolio. The Company is one of the largest mineral resource holders in the state with a pipeline of high-grade multi-stage projects strategically located in Nevada's most prolific gold-producing trends. Leveraging its central processing facility following an anticipated refurbishment, i-80 Gold is executing a hub-and-spoke regional mining and processing strategy to maximize efficiency and growth. i-80 Gold's shares are listed on the NYSE (NYSE: IAUX) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: IAU). For more information, visit www.i80gold.com.
